- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 2 negative values in recent history), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope in the following 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive but price history shows strong mean reversion, model tends to overestimate continuation; apply a 2–5% downward bias to mid-term forecasts.
- When sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model often overestimates momentum; cap forecast growth at 3–5% above recent 7-day average to avoid overbought bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates downward corrections after negative sentiment; add 1–3% upward bias to early forecast days if sentiment is negative or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative swings, model tends to lag in recognizing reversal; shift forecast 1–2 days earlier to align with sentiment momentum.
